The formalism not only states the count; it proves the finiteness the paper claims it cannot see, which is why its axioms never demanded the surplus the paper charges. An algebraic-QFT referee will read this sentence as the tell that the authors have not engaged the literature their own footnotes cite.
batch_verdicts.fix: Engage Buchholz–Wichmann nuclearity and Casini head-on: replace 'the formalism cannot state the count' with an honest account of the counting structures inside axiomatic QFT, and explain why the paper's census survives them — or accept that it does not.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: The quoted sentence is confirmed defective and the paper's own citation list convicts it: Buchholz–Wichmann nuclearity (Commun. Math. Phys. 106, 1986) is precisely a count of local degrees of freedom below an energy cutoff, formulated and adopted inside the axiomatic framework as a selection criterion; and Casini's relative-entropy Bekenstein bound is the paper's own reference [8], leaned on twice (§2, §11) as 'a theorem of relative entropy within quantum field theory.' The paper cannot cite Casini as its state meter and simultaneously declare the count 'invisible' to Casini's formalism — 'there is no census... the notion of a distinguishable cell does not exist in the formalism' is false as written and an algebraic-QFT referee will treat it exactly as the finding predicts. That half is confirmed. But the attack's closing inference — 'the formalism... proves the finiteness the paper claims it cannot see, which is why its axioms never demanded the surplus the paper charges' — overreaches and fails, and this is where the finding must be cut down: (i) the prize demands Wightman/OS strength, and neither nuclearity nor the split property is among those axioms — they are additional selection criteria bolted on precisely to tame what the bare axioms permit; (ii) the bare axioms DO demand the surplus — local algebras of type III, operator-valued distributions at every scale, sharp-region entanglement entropy divergent; (iii) Casini's finiteness is a statement about vacuum-SUBTRACTED relative entropy, and its construction concedes on its face that the unsubtracted census diverges — it does not make the region's raw state count finite. So the formalism's counting instruments recover finiteness by installing an energy meter and subtracting the divergent surplus, which is grist for the paper's thesis, not against it: Lemma 2, Theorem 1, and the surplus charge are untouched. batch_verdicts.quote: We prove that the existence demanded by the Yang–Mills problem — a quantum gauge theory on continuum ℝ⁴, satisfying axioms of Wightman or Osterwalder–Schrader strength — is a supertask: it requires the instantiation of infinitely many distinguishable physical degrees of freedom in every bounded region, and the completion of infinitely many refinement stages in any construction of the object.
batch_verdicts.attack: Equivocation between mathematical and physical existence, and the paper's own text supplies the refutation. The Clay demand — which §10 concedes is taken 'exactly' from Jaffe–Witten's 'sober mathematics' — is a demand for a THEOREM: a mathematical construction of a structure satisfying axioms. A supertask is a physical process; existence claims are not processes, and mathematical constructions are not resource-priced by Margolus–Levitin — a proof is a finite string, and limits are taken by quantifiers, not by sequential energy-funded stages (Earman–Norton/Butterfield supertask literature is explicit on this). The paper itself proves the point twice over: free fields satisfying the Wightman axioms were constructed decades ago with finite ink, and §8 states in so many words that 'the one time the supertask was actually finished, with full rigor' — Aizenman–Duminil-Copin completed a four-dimensional continuum limit. If two mathematicians finished it, it is not the unperformable supertask of Theorem 1; if what they finished was 'merely mathematical,' then the Clay demand is merely mathematical and Theorem 1 does not engage it. Either horn destroys the abstract's first sentence. The same equivocation runs the other way for the lattice: 'finite integrals whose existence is inspection' is mathematical existence when it favors the counting formulation, but existence is required to mean physical instantiation when indicting the continuum — one word, two standards, chosen per side. The §11 finitism response concedes the killing premise ('No theorem of continuum mathematics is disputed anywhere in this paper'): then a Wightman–Yang–Mills existence theorem, if proved tomorrow, is likewise undisputed, and nothing in this paper bears on the problem as posed. §10's warrant-dilemma is the paper's only defense and it fails: a motivational sentence about laboratories in the prize's public description does not convert a formal theorem-demand into a physical-instantiation demand; the Balaban 'supertask in analyst's clothing' reading is the same error — Balaban's stall is a difficulty of proving uniformity, an analysis problem, not an energy budget, and analysts are not bounded by πℏ/2E in the relevant sense.
batch_verdicts.fix: Retreat explicitly and globally to the claim actually proved: physical instantiation of the axioms' census is impossible (Theorem 1), and therefore the physical reading of the prize's warrant fails — the dilemma of §10 becomes the thesis, not a corollary. Strike or restrict 'any construction of the object completes infinitely many refinement stages' to physical processes; stop calling mathematical existence a supertask (rename the target 'instantiation-as-posed'); rewrite the abstract's first sentence and the subtitle accordingly; and add a §11 objection stating this attack in full strength with the retreat as the answer.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Defense attempted: the paper's lexicon arguably makes 'construction' physical throughout (Lemma 2's 'instantiated' is a physical object's state; section 2 frames the two clauses as physical process and physical state), and the considered position already contains the retreat — section 10 poses the warrant-dilemma, section 12 explicitly concedes a future rigorous construction 'would not contradict this paper's physical claims,' and section 13 returns the notation-question to its owners. But the defense cannot save the indicted sentences. (i) The abstract's first sentence predicates a physical-process property (supertask, resource-priced stages) of 'the existence demanded by the Yang-Mills problem' — which section 10 says is taken 'exactly' from Jaffe-Witten's 'sober mathematics,' a theorem-demand; a proof is a finite string, limits are taken by quantifiers, so 'any construction of the object completes infinitely many refinement stages' is false of mathematical construction, and the free fields (Wightman-satisfying, finite ink) are standing counterexamples. (ii) The paper's own section 8 supplies the internal contradiction: 'the one time the supertask was actually finished, with full rigor' calls Aizenman-Duminil-Copin's mathematical completion a supertask — if 'supertask' is univocally physical (the only reading Theorem 1 supports), that sentence is false; if it covers mathematical completion, Theorem 1 does not bar it. Either way the abstract's headline cannot stand as written. (iii) The Balaban 'supertask in analyst's clothing' reading is an analogy in prosecutorial voice — the stall at uniformity is an analysis difficulty, not an energy budget; on the lab's grading ladder it is a Reading presented as if Forced. The attack overreaches only in 'nothing in this paper bears on the problem as posed' — the section 10 dilemma about the prize's warrant survives the retreat intact. But the required change is global (abstract first sentence, subtitle, section 1 First, section 8 wording) and mandatory, so the finding is confirmed rather than partial: the surgery is survivable, and it is surgery.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Four coordinated edits. (1) Abstract, first sentence, replace with: 'We prove that the object demanded by the Yang-Mills problem — a quantum gauge theory on continuum R^4, satisfying axioms of Wightman or Osterwalder-Schrader strength — is physically uninstantiable: its axioms require infinitely many distinguishable physical degrees of freedom in every bounded region, and any physical realization of its refinement structure is a supertask. Whether the object exists as mathematics is not disputed here; what is proved is that no physical system is, or could be, the object the axioms describe — and that the problem's empirical warrant therefore attaches to a different object than its existence demand.' (2) Section 1, First claim: change 'any construction of such an object completes infinitely many refinement stages' to 'any physical realization of such an object completes infinitely many refinement stages'; adjust subtitle from 'Continuum existence is a supertask' to 'Continuum instantiation is a supertask' (or 'Continuum existence is a supertask for anything physical'). (3) Section 8: replace 'the one time the supertask was actually finished, with full rigor' with 'the one time the limit was actually completed, with full rigor' — reserving 'supertask' strictly for the physical reading, as Theorem 1 requires; likewise soften the Balaban passage to a reading ('the stall sits exactly where the count says every physical execution would halt — an alignment this paper reads as diagnostic, not a theorem'). (4) Add a section 11 objection stating this attack at full strength ('mathematical existence is not a process; a proof is a finite string; free fields already satisfy the axioms by theorem') and answer it with the retreat as the thesis: Theorem 1 targets instantiation; the paper's claim on the mathematical problem is confined to the section 10 dilemma about its warrant; section 12's concession is cross-referenced. This makes the abstract consistent with what sections 10, 12 and 13 already hold.

batch_verdicts.section: §2 (Axiom S is a theorem of the indicted notation); §11 (finitism and Poincaré responses)
batch_verdicts.quote: The claim is about physical instantiation, and its instruments are two theorems of physics, not of philosophy. … its *exact* content is an axiom about the completed census — Lemma 2 — and inherits the census's status.
batch_verdicts.attack: The paper's meters are theorems OF the continuum formalism it declares physically empty, and the paper supplies no criterion for which theorems of that notation retain physical authority. Margolus–Levitin is proved from continuous-time Schrödinger evolution on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space — the predecessor NS paper openly says so ('holds on continuous spacetime with continuous Schrödinger evolution'); this paper drops even that acknowledgment. Casini's bound is derived in continuum QFT using the modular Hamiltonian of the Rindler wedge, whose identification with the boost generator requires EXACT Lorentz boost invariance — and the paper's own §11 Poincaré response grades exact Lorentz invariance as 'an axiom about the completed census' that 'inherits the census's status,' i.e., the status of unfalsifiable notation. By the paper's own grading, then, Axiom S is derived from a census-status premise: the paper's objection machinery demotes its own state meter. Calling both instruments 'theorems of physics, not of philosophy' assumes precisely what the hostile referee denies — that some consequences of the continuum notation are physical truths while others (infinitely many DOF per region) are empty surplus — and the paper nowhere states the demarcation that sorts them. Corollary 5's own logic (only finite-precision consequences are empirical) cannot rescue Axiom S, because the 2πER/ℏc form is not a theorem of any finite-depth lattice theory (lattice region entropy is sites × log dim, unrelated to ER; the constant comes from continuum wedge modular theory). The fallback in §2/§11 — 'the process clause alone carries' — is anticipated but does not cover: without Axiom S the paper loses 'existence as a state,' the only prong that even faces a standing object rather than a construction process, which the previous findings show is the only prong that could matter.
batch_verdicts.fix: Add a §11 objection titled, in substance, 'your meters are theorems of the notation you indict,' and answer it with an explicit criterion: e.g., ML survives on every finite-dimensional substrate (provable, and worth a test in the suite), whereas Casini's bound is continuum-native — then either downgrade Axiom S to a consistency check the continuum imposes on itself, or honestly carry the state clause as conditional. Reconcile the Poincaré response with Casini's boost-invariance premise or amend one of them.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Defense attempted on three fronts, two partially successful, none decisive. (i) The claim that the paper 'drops even that acknowledgment' about Margolus-Levitin slightly overstates: YM section 1 says 'No appeal is made to a fundamental lattice, to speculative microphysics, or to any discreteness of spacetime,' which carries similar content to the NS paper's 'holds on continuous spacetime with continuous Schrodinger evolution' (NS section 11); and ML itself is only mildly continuum-native (continuous time; its proof does not need infinite-dimensionality and survives on every finite-dimensional substrate — the attacker's own proposed criterion concedes this). (ii) Corollary 5 supplies an implicit demarcation the attack underweights: physical iff finite-precision-consequence-bearing; under it Axiom S classifies as an empirical claim while the surplus does not, so a univocal criterion is available to the paper. But (iii) the central collision is real and I could not break it: Casini's 2*pi*E*R/(hbar*c) form requires the Rindler-wedge modular Hamiltonian to be the boost generator (Bisognano-Wichmann), which requires exact Lorentz boost invariance as a hypothesis — and section 11's Poincare response grades exact invariance as 'an axiom about the completed census' that 'inherits the census's status.' The paper's own objection machinery thereby demotes the premise of its state meter while section 2 and section 11 call Axiom S 'a theorem of physics, not of philosophy.' The 2*pi*E*R/(hbar*c) form is indeed not a theorem of any finite-depth lattice theory (lattice region entropy is sites times log dim, unrelated to E*R). And the anticipated fallback — 'the process clause alone carries' — fails by the paper's own architecture: section 2 assigns the state clause to 'existence as a state,' the only prong that faces a standing object rather than a construction process, so dropping Axiom S deletes the face of the demand that matters most. The paper must state its criterion and reconcile the Poincare response with Axiom S's derivation; the finding's severity grade (serious, not fatal) is fair.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Three edits. (1) Add a section 11 objection: 'Objection: the paper's meters are theorems of the very notation it indicts — Margolus-Levitin is proved in continuum quantum mechanics, and Casini's form of the Bekenstein bound is derived in continuum QFT from the exact boost invariance this paper's own Poincare response grades as census-status notation.' Answer with an explicit criterion: a bound retains physical authority when its content is a finite-precision constraint on distinguishable structure and it survives on every finite-depth substrate. Margolus-Levitin passes — the orthogonalization floor pi*hbar/2E holds verbatim for every finite-dimensional quantum system (provable; add a test to the suite). Casini's 2*pi*E*R/(hbar*c) form is continuum-native; therefore present Axiom S for what it is: the notation's own self-audit — the indicted formalism's own theorem that a finite-energy region holds finitely many nats of distinguishable structure — wielded against the notation's census on the opponent's premises, and carried as conditional. (2) Amend the section 2 warrant of Axiom S accordingly: after the Casini citation add 'The bound is derived within the continuum formalism, exact Poincare invariance included; this paper uses it as the continuum's own concession, and the unconditional conclusion rests on the process clause' — and amend section 11's Bekenstein response to stop calling the state clause merely a sharpener while section 2 calls it the answer to existence-as-a-state: either downgrade section 2's two-faces architecture to process-primary, or carry the state face explicitly as the conditional, notation-internal prong. (3) Reconcile the Poincare response: change 'inherits the census's status' to language that distinguishes the exactness hypothesis (census-status as an empirical claim about nature) from theorems derived under it (which retain conditional authority and, where finite-precision-testable, empirical standing under Corollary 5's own demarcation).

batch_verdicts.quote: The distinctive content of the continuum hypothesis — actually infinitely many degrees of freedom in a bounded region, as against finitely many — entails no finite-precision observable consequence: every finite dataset consistent with the continuum is consistent with its denial. … Twice in the history of physics the infinite-modes commitment has yielded an indirect observable consequence, and both times the consequence was catastrophic.
batch_verdicts.attack: The paper asserts that the continuum commitment is unfalsifiable in principle (Corollary 5, and §12: 'The rival commitment, for its part, can name no observation that would refute it') AND that it was twice refuted by observation (§1, §9: 'catastrophically wrong on both occasions it acquired an indirect one'). A commitment no possible observation can bear on cannot have been marked to market by measurement twice; the paper wants both the Popperian conviction (not empirical) and the empirical conviction (refuted), and the word 'indirect' — nowhere defined — carries the entire load. The obvious repair (the catastrophes refute the continuum only in conjunction with auxiliaries: equipartition; gravity coupling to zero-point energy) is Duhem–Quine, and it cuts symmetrically: the finite-depth commitment is equally unfalsifiable modulo auxiliaries, which dissolves §12's claimed asymmetry ('The thesis is falsifiable, and asymmetrically so against its rival'). The NS predecessor contains the same structure in milder form (one catastrophe); this paper doubles the exposure and sharpens the contradiction by declaring the 10¹²³ item a live 'quantitative failure' — a currently outstanding empirical consequence of the allegedly consequence-free commitment. No §11 objection addresses it.
batch_verdicts.fix: Define direct vs indirect consequence precisely (e.g., Corollary 5 covers consequences within the fixed theory's observables; the catastrophes arise when the mode census is coupled to a new sector), restate Corollary 5 as 'no direct consequence,' and confront the Duhemian symmetry explicitly in §12 — or move the two catastrophes out of the epistemic-status argument entirely and present them as historical motivation only.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Defense attempted: the paper is not oblivious to the distinction — section 9's closing sentence already carries the correctly scoped form ('unfalsifiable in every direct test, and catastrophically wrong on both occasions it acquired an indirect one'), and the abstract does label the two catastrophes 'indirect.' So the intended structure (direct consequences within the fixed theory's observables vs. consequences of coupling the mode census to a new sector) is visible in the text, and the repair is a consistency-and-definition pass, not a retraction. But the finding's core stands: three quoted statements overreach beyond that scoping and are jointly inconsistent with the twice-marked-to-market claim as written — the abstract's 'unfalsifiable in principle,' Corollary 5's flat 'entails no finite-precision observable consequence: every finite dataset consistent with the continuum is consistent with its denial,' and section 12's 'The rival commitment, for its part, can name no observation that would refute it.' Section 13 then asserts 'its surplus content has twice been marked to market.' A commitment with no observable consequence whatsoever cannot have been refuted by measurement twice; 'indirect' does carry the entire load and is nowhere defined; and no section 11 objection addresses it. The Duhem point also has real teeth: the natural repair (catastrophes refute the census only jointly with auxiliaries — equipartition; gravity coupling to zero-point energy) does cut both ways, so section 12's asymmetry claim needs an explicit argument — though the attack slightly overstates dissolution, since the count's falsifiers include a direct in-principle test (a Margolus-Levitin violation) while the continuum's exhibits are auxiliary-mediated, so a scoped asymmetry survives if argued. The paper must define the distinction, rescope the three statements, and face Duhem; confirmed at the stated severity.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: (1) At Corollary 5, define the distinction and rescope: 'Call a consequence direct when it is an observable of the fixed theory at finite precision; indirect when the mode census is coupled to a further sector — thermal equilibrium in the cavity, gravity for the vacuum — so that the census's cardinality itself enters the prediction. Theorem 3 covers the direct ledger: the surplus entails no direct finite-precision consequence.' (2) Abstract: change 'is unfalsifiable in principle' to 'is unfalsifiable in every direct test' (matching section 9's own closer). (3) Section 12: replace 'The rival commitment, for its part, can name no observation that would refute it' with 'The rival commitment can name no direct observation that would refute it; on the two occasions its census acquired an indirect consequence, measurement went against it, and the remaining defense — blaming the auxiliary rather than the census — is available to any commitment whatsoever, which is why this paper stakes the asymmetry on the direct ledger, where the count names its falsifiers (a Margolus-Levitin or Bekenstein violation is a direct test) and the continuum, by Corollary 5, can name none.' (4) Alternatively, if the Duhemian paragraph is unwanted, move the two catastrophes out of the epistemic-status argument into section 1 as historical motivation only, and let Corollary 5 stand alone — but then section 13's 'twice been marked to market' must be softened to match.

batch_verdicts.quote: The physics of the gauge field is counting all the way through; it never used the object the problem demands.
batch_verdicts.attack: Self-undermining by the paper's own star citation. The percent-precision hadron masses of Dürr et al. [10] are obtained only after continuum extrapolation — simulations at several spacings extrapolated to a→0 — and the running coupling 'matched to experiment' is quoted in continuum MS-bar; the lattice industry defines its published physical numbers as estimates OF the continuum-limit value, treating finite-spacing results as instrument artifacts to be removed. So the empirical warrant for 'nothing empirical is lost' operationally routes through the very limit the paper declares uninstantiable notation, and 'never used' is false as stated. This matters structurally: §10's category-error charge and warrant-severing dilemma depend on the claim that the laboratories' numbers were computed without the continuum object, but the practitioners' own procedure identifies the physical prediction with the a→0 value — the identification the paper calls a fifty-year conflation is enacted in the methods section of its own reference. §11's scaffold objection addresses ontological priority (which formulation is fundamental) and §7 gestures at the scaling window ('results become spacing-independent in dimensionless combinations'), but neither engages the operational fact that spacing-independence fails at the quoted precision — which is exactly why [10] extrapolates.
batch_verdicts.fix: Replace 'never used the object the problem demands' with a defensible claim: the computations never used an axiomatically complete continuum theory, and continuum extrapolation is finite arithmetic on finitely many data points estimating the scaling-window plateau — then argue explicitly why the extrapolated target's empirical primacy does not concede the continuum's physical standing, and add this as a named objection in §11.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: The factual core is true and I verified its quantitative basis: Durr et al. compute at several spacings and extrapolate to a=0 — at their spacings (roughly 0.065-0.125 fm) the discretization scale (a*Lambda)^2 runs about 1-4 percent, the same order as the quoted precision, so continuum extrapolation is genuinely load-bearing for the percent-precision claim; and alpha_s is published in continuum MS-bar, a scheme defined via dimensional regularization. The paper nowhere preempts this, section 11's scaffold objection addresses ontological priority rather than the operational practice, and section 7's 'results become spacing-independent in dimensionless combinations' is loose at exactly the precision the paper quotes. A named objection is owed. But the headline inference overshoots, which is why this is partial rather than confirmed. 'Never used the object the problem demands' is defensible under the paper's precise referent: the object the problem demands is an axiomatically complete Wightman/Osterwalder-Schrader theory, and continuum extrapolation uses no such object — it is finite arithmetic (a polynomial fit in a^2) on finitely many finite-depth data points, estimating a limit of individual numbers, a far weaker commitment than the axiomatic object, and one that would make sense even if the full axiomatic theory failed to exist. Since the paper explicitly disputes no theorem of continuum mathematics, invoking a numerical limit as calibration target is consistent with its thesis; hence 'false as stated' and 'section 10's category-error charge loses its factual premise' are overstated — the premise survives in rescoped form, which the attacker's own proposed fix concedes by supplying exactly that rescoped claim. What is confirmed: the rhetoric ('counting all the way through,' 'never used') invites the referee's misreading, the distinction between the axiomatic object and the numerical limit is absent from the text, and section 7 needs the corrections clause.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: (1) Section 1, Second claim, and section 6: replace 'The physics of the gauge field is counting all the way through; it never used the object the problem demands' with 'The physics of the gauge field is counting all the way through: no ab-initio number ever issued from an axiomatically complete continuum theory, because none exists to issue from. What the practice does use is the far edge of the scaling window — results at several finite spacings, extrapolated by finite arithmetic on finitely many points to the a->0 plateau. The extrapolation estimates a limit of numbers; it neither requires nor invokes the axiomatic object whose existence the prize demands.' (2) Section 7, Instrumental: change 'the regime in which lattice results become spacing-independent in dimensionless combinations' to 'the regime in which lattice results become spacing-independent in dimensionless combinations up to corrections vanishing as powers of the spacing — corrections the practice removes by extrapolation.' (3) Add a section 11 objection: 'Objection: the lattice's published numbers are continuum-extrapolated, and the running coupling is quoted in a continuum scheme; the practice defines the physical value as the a->0 limit, so the empirical warrant routes through the continuum after all.' Answer: the extrapolation is finite arithmetic on finite-depth data; the limit it estimates is a limit of observables, not the axiomatic object; the identification of the physical value with the plateau is precisely the scaling-window claim this paper endorses; and no step of the procedure instantiates, or presupposes the instantiability of, the completed census — the only thing Theorem 1 bars. (4) Rebuild section 10's premise on the rescoped sentence so the category-error charge cites 'no axiomatically complete continuum theory was used' rather than 'the continuum was never used.'

batch_verdicts.quote: The precedent does not decide the Yang–Mills case; it assigns the burden. Those who assert that the completed census houses the physics owe an example in which it ever has.
batch_verdicts.attack: The demanded examples exist and are the founding results of constructive QFT — catalogued in the paper's own reference [2]. P(φ)₂ satisfies the Wightman axioms with definite-mass particles and a NONTRIVIAL scattering matrix (Glimm-Jaffe-Spencer, Ann. Math. 100 (1974); Osterwalder-Sénéor 1976); φ⁴₃ is a quartic Wightman QFT on R³ (Glimm-Jaffe 1973; Feldman-Osterwalder, Ann. Phys. 97 (1976)); the 2D abelian Higgs model satisfies the OS axioms with a mass gap (Brydges-Fröhlich-Seiler; Balaban-Brydges-Imbrie-Jaffe) — Jaffe-Witten call it 'the only complete example of an interacting gauge theory satisfying the axioms.' Each is a rigorously completed continuum limit in which the interaction survived; and by the paper's own dimension-blind census (Lemma 2 reads 'operator-valued distributions at every scale' as the completed ledger; Theorem 1′ bars 'infinitely many distinguishable degrees of freedom in a bounded region' with no reference to d=4), each is a completed 'supertask' that housed the physics. The only shield is the word 'four-dimensional' in §8's 'the only experimental datum mathematics possesses about what completed four-dimensional supertasks deliver' — a restriction nowhere justified inside the counting framework, which does not distinguish dimensions. §12 compounds it: the demanded account 'of how uniformity over infinitely many octaves was purchased,' which 'five decades of the best constructive analysis has not produced,' was in fact produced repeatedly in d=2,3, including genuinely renormalizable infinitely-many-scales cases (φ⁴₃, Gross-Neveu₂). A referee will conclude the paper either does not know the constructive canon or has suppressed it — and will note the irony that the same document the paper mines for its 'concession' ([2]) contains the refuting catalog. Either reading dismisses §§8, 11-12 as argued.
batch_verdicts.fix: Cite the d=2,3 constructions explicitly and concede that rigorously completed continuum limits can and do retain their interactions. Restate the φ⁴₄ precedent as bearing on the marginal, non-asymptotically-free case in d=4 only, and supply an actual argument (currently absent) for why the d=4 class is the relevant reference class for the burden-shift — e.g., marginality/renormalizability — rather than letting the 'four-dimensional' qualifier do the work silently.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Defense attempted and failed. (1) Context-scoping: the burden sentence sits inside the phi-4 objection, whose preceding sentence carries the 'four-dimensional' qualifier, so one could argue d=4 is implied. But 'an example in which it ever has' is grammatically universal, the sentence states a general epistemic principle ('it assigns the burden'), and Section 12 repeats the unqualified form ('which Section 8 shows five decades of the best constructive analysis has not produced... how uniformity over infinitely many octaves was purchased'). (2) Reading 'houses the physics' as physical instantiation: fails, because Section 8's parallel phrase ('emptied of the physics it was built to house') is unambiguously about the mathematical limit retaining its interaction, and under that reading P(phi)2 (Wightman axioms + mass gap + nontrivial S-matrix, Glimm-Jaffe-Spencer Ann. Math. 100 (1974); Osterwalder-Senor 1976), phi-4 in d=3 (Glimm-Jaffe; Feldman-Osterwalder Ann. Phys. 97 (1976); Magnen-Senor), the 2D abelian Higgs model (OS axioms + gap, Brydges-Frohlich-Seiler 1979), and asymptotically free Gross-Neveu-2 (Gawedzki-Kupiainen CMP 102 (1985); Feldman-Magnen-Rivasseau-Senor) are direct counterexamples: rigorously completed continuum limits whose interactions survived. (3) The deepest cut is correct and undefendable: the paper's own counting is dimension-blind by design — Theorem 1-prime says 'no octree, no gauge group, and no geometry' — so the framework supplies no internal reason to privilege d=4, and the 'four-dimensional' qualifier does silent, unjustified work exactly where the burden is assigned. Gross-Neveu-2 is especially damaging to the Section 12 clause: it is an asymptotically free, marginal-coupling theory whose infinite-scale uniformity WAS rigorously purchased — so 'constructive analysis has not produced' the account is false unless scoped to d=4. Two edges of the attack overstate: (a) 'Either reading dismisses Sections 8, 11-12 as argued' is too strong — Section 8's own load-bearing sentences carry the four-dimensional qualifier, Section 13 says 'the one completed limit in the dimension,' and the paper's physical-instantiation thesis ('We do not claim the continuum is inconsistent as mathematics') is untouched by mathematical completions in any dimension; (b) phi-4 in d=3 is super-renormalizable, not 'genuinely renormalizable' — Gross-Neveu-2 carries that weight alone; and the quoted Jaffe-Witten phrase about the 2D Higgs model should be verified verbatim before being echoed. None of this rescues the two sentences as written. The paper stakes its authority on candor and on inviting attack; omitting the constructive canon while citing [2], which catalogs it, is exactly the exposure the finding names. Paper must change.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Three repairs. (A) In Section 11, replace 'The precedent does not decide the Yang-Mills case; it assigns the burden. Those who assert that the completed census houses the physics owe an example in which it ever has.' with: 'The precedent does not decide the Yang-Mills case; it assigns a burden, and the burden must be scoped honestly. batch_verdicts.section: §8 · Why the continuum cannot decide its own question (and Abstract)
batch_verdicts.quote: In 2021 Aizenman and Duminil-Copin closed a sixty-year question by proving that the four-dimensional φ⁴ theory — the only interacting four-dimensional field theory whose continuum limit has ever been rigorously completed — is trivial: the limit is a free field [19].
batch_verdicts.attack: Three defects a hostile referee will stack. (i) 'Completed' misdescribes a triviality theorem: Aizenman-Duminil-Copin proved a no-go — every (subsequential) scaling limit of the models is Gaussian. Nobody completed the continuum limit of an interacting 4D theory; the appositive is self-refuting, since if the limit is free it is not the completed limit of an 'interacting four-dimensional field theory' in any sense that does the paper's work. The abstract repeats the defect ('the one interacting four-dimensional continuum limit ever completed with full rigor'). (ii) Scope: the theorem covers nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising and lattice φ⁴ on Z⁴ — the reflection-positive class with a random-current representation; ADC themselves leave non-reflection-positive and long-range regularizations open, so 'the four-dimensional φ⁴ theory... is trivial,' stated flat, overreaches the theorem. (iii) 'Only... ever': Gawedzki-Kupiainen's asymptotically free wrong-sign φ⁴₄ (CMP 99, 1985) is a rigorously controlled 4D continuum limit with non-Gaussian correlations; it fails OS positivity and so can be excluded — but only by a qualifier the sentence does not contain, and Rivasseau-school referees will raise it. A careful referee will also expect acknowledgment of the 2024 Annals corrigendum to [19].
batch_verdicts.fix: Reword to something like: 'the one four-dimensional case in which the interacting scaling-limit question has been rigorously settled — for the nearest-neighbor reflection-positive class — and the verdict was Gaussian.' Apply the same repair to the abstract's clause; add the scope qualifier and cite the corrigendum (Ann. Math. 199 (2024)).
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Defense attempted; the sentence needs repair on all three prongs, though prong (i)'s framing is inflated. (i) 'Self-refuting' overstates: the recoverable meaning — the scaling limit of the interacting lattice family was rigorously settled and came out free — is exactly the precedent the paper needs, the very next clause ('is trivial: the limit is a free field') prevents any reader from being misled, and the attack's own proposed rewording preserves the precedent's full argumentative weight, conceding that the role survives. But the appositive as written ('the only interacting four-dimensional field theory whose continuum limit has ever been rigorously completed') is genuinely defective wording: Aizenman-Duminil-Copin proved a Gaussianity theorem about all (subsequential) scaling limits — a verdict, not a construction — and 'The scaling limit exists; the axioms are satisfied' glosses the theorem's actual form. Precision costs nothing and the loose word hands a hostile referee a free jab at the paper's most load-bearing citation. (ii) Scope: correct and undefendable — the theorem covers the nearest-neighbor reflection-positive lattice class on Z^4 (the random-current/infrared-bound machinery requires it), and 'the four-dimensional phi-4 theory is trivial,' stated flat, outruns the proved statement; non-reflection-positive and long-range regularizations remain open by ADC's own account. (iii) 'Only... ever': correct in substance — the negative-coupling (asymptotically free) phi-4-4 of Gawedzki-Kupiainen is a rigorously controlled four-dimensional limit with non-Gaussian correlations, excluded only because it fails OS positivity/stability, a qualifier the sentence does not contain; Rivasseau-school referees raise it routinely. One citation correction to the attack itself: CMP 99 (1985) 197 is the infrared counterpart (massless lattice theory at fixed spacing — verified via Springer abstract); the wrong-sign continuum-limit construction is the companion paper 'Non-trivial continuum limit of a phi-4-4 model with negative coupling constant' (Nucl. Phys. B, 1985) — the repair should cite that one. (iv) The corrigendum is real and verified: Ann. Math. 199, issue 1 (2024), DOI 10.4007/annals.2024.199.1.7 (projecteuclid.org); a paper whose titlenote advertises mechanical re-verification on every revision cannot cite the 2021 theorem without its published correction. All named locations (abstract and Section 8) must change; verdict CONFIRMED, with the note that the repairs strengthen rather than weaken the paper's use of the precedent.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Four repairs. (A) Section 8, replace the sentence with: 'In 2021 Aizenman and Duminil-Copin closed a sixty-year question by proving that the scaling limits of the four-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising and lattice phi-4 models — the reflection-positive class, and the only four-dimensional case in which the interacting scaling-limit question has ever been rigorously settled within axioms of the strength at issue — are Gaussian: every limit the interacting family possesses is a free field [19].' And replace 'The scaling limit exists; the axioms are satisfied; and the interaction did not survive the completion.' with 'The limits exist; the free field satisfies the axioms; the interaction did not survive the passage.' (B) Abstract, replace 'the one interacting four-dimensional continuum limit ever completed with full rigor, phi-4 (Aizenman-Duminil-Copin, 2021), returned a free field' with 'the one four-dimensional interacting scaling-limit question ever rigorously settled — nearest-neighbor reflection-positive phi-4 and Ising (Aizenman-Duminil-Copin, 2021) — was answered with a free field'. (C) Add after the Section 8 sentence a one-clause acknowledgment: 'One qualifier is owed and given: the negative-coupling phi-4-4 of Gawedzki and Kupiainen (1985) is a rigorously controlled four-dimensional limit with non-Gaussian correlations; it fails Osterwalder-Schrader positivity and is therefore no candidate for the axioms the problem demands.' — citing Gawedzki-Kupiainen, Non-trivial continuum limit of a phi-4-4 model with negative coupling constant, Nucl. Phys. B (1985), with CMP 99 (1985) 197 as the infrared companion (verify volume/page at press time). (D) Amend reference [19] to append: '; Corrigendum: Ann. Math. 199 (1) (2024), DOI 10.4007/annals.2024.199.1.7.'

batch_verdicts.quote: Every ab-initio number the strong interaction has ever supplied to experiment was computed on the counting side of the ledger. There is no competing set of numbers from the continuum construction, because the continuum construction does not exist — that absence being, precisely, the problem statement's own concession [2].
batch_verdicts.attack: Factually false, and the falsehood is load-bearing for §10. Perturbative continuum QCD — dimensional regularization on ℝ⁴, no lattice, no depth cutoff, no counting instrument — has produced ab-initio, experimentally confirmed numbers for fifty years: the R-ratio in e⁺e⁻ annihilation, DIS scaling violations via DGLAP evolution, jet cross sections at NNLO, event shapes, the τ hadronic width, the running of α_s itself. These, not the lattice hadron spectrum, constitute the bulk of the 'tested at many experimental laboratories' warrant the prize text cites (the 2004 Nobel for asymptotic freedom rests on them). §11's renormalization objection ('impose a cutoff — a finite depth') does not cover dimensional regularization, which is not a mode count and imposes no depth. §10's prosecution — 'The predictions the laboratories tested were computed on the counting formulation' — inherits the falsehood, so the category-error charge loses its factual premise as stated. The paper equivocates between 'the axiomatically constructed continuum theory' (which indeed does not exist and produced no numbers) and 'continuum methods' (which produced thousands).
batch_verdicts.fix: Rescope every occurrence to 'every ab-initio nonperturbative number', explicitly concede the perturbative continuum record, and either claim it for the count via an honest argument (dim reg is not obviously octave bookkeeping — the current renormalization objection does not stretch to it) or rebuild §10's premise on the nonperturbative sector alone.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: The factual core is right: perturbative continuum QCD (dim reg, no lattice, no depth cutoff) supplied a large share of the laboratory record the prize's warrant cites — R-ratio, DGLAP scaling violations, jet cross sections, the four-loop-verified running of alpha_s — and the flat universal 'Every ab-initio number... was computed on the counting side of the ledger' (§6, echoed in abstract and §2-intro) is indefensible as written unless 'ab initio' is silently read as the lattice term of art (Dürr et al.'s own title), a restriction the paper never states and whose argumentative use ('counting all the way through; it never used the object') exceeds. The §11 renormalization objection ('impose a cutoff — a finite depth') genuinely does not cover dimensional regularization, which imposes no depth. BUT the structural claim fails: §10's category-error charge does not lose its premise, because the charge needs only that no laboratory-tested number came from an object of Wightman/OS strength — and the attack itself concedes the axiomatic theory 'produced no numbers.' Perturbative QCD is an asymptotic series that constructs no such object (Jaffe–Witten's text is motivated by exactly that gap), takes nonperturbative inputs (PDFs, one alpha_s calibration) from measurement, and its scheme-independent one-loop content is Lemma 1 itself. §10 also already hedges ('and in the asymptotic octaves'). Defect real, collapse claim wrong.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Three edits. (1) §6: 'Every ab-initio nonperturbative number the strong interaction has ever supplied to experiment was computed on the counting side of the ledger. The perturbative record — the R-ratio, the scaling violations, the jet cross sections, the running of the coupling verified to four loops — is conceded in full and claims nothing for the demanded object: it is an asymptotic series organized by the renormalization flow of Lemma 1, it takes its nonperturbative inputs from measurement, and it constructs no object of Wightman strength — the problem statement's own motivation for demanding one [2].' Mirror 'nonperturbative' in the abstract and §1-Second. (2) §11 renormalization objection, extend: 'Dimensional regularization removes the mode count from the intermediate bookkeeping, not from the physics: its outputs are statements of scale dependence governed by the same flow, its scheme-independent one-loop coefficient is the octave rate of Lemma 1, and no one claims the dim-reg series defines the theory — the problem statement exists because it does not.' (3) §10: '...were computed on the counting formulation or by a perturbative series that constructs no continuum object — in neither case on the object the prize demands.'

batch_verdicts.quote: the zero-point energy of the continuum mode family, cut off only at the Planck scale, exceeds the observed vacuum energy density by a factor of order 10¹²³ [15] — machine-verified in the accompanying suite — the largest quantitative discrepancy between a theoretical expectation and a measurement in the history of science.
batch_verdicts.attack: The sentence indicts itself: 'cut off only at the Planck scale' means the 10¹²³ is computed from a FINITE mode census — precisely the depth-≈66 ledger this paper endorses as physical. The uncut continuum prediction is not 10¹²³ but infinity; the 10¹²³ bill is owed by any finite counting theory with a Planck-depth ledger, and even a cutoff at the confinement scale overshoots the observed vacuum density by ~10⁴⁴. The catastrophe therefore does not discriminate the continuum from the count and cannot serve as the second 'indirect observable consequence' of the infinite-modes commitment — on the paper's own accounting it stands on the count's books too, and 'standing on the continuum's books to this day' (abstract) is exactly backwards. Additionally, [15] (Weinberg 1989) predates the 1998 measurement of Λ; Weinberg's figure against the then-available observational bound is ~10¹¹⁸, so the citation cannot carry the 10¹²³ claim as scoped.
batch_verdicts.fix: Retire the vacuum catastrophe as an exhibit against the infinite-modes commitment, or add the honest concession that the 10¹²³ arises in the cutoff (finite-census) theory and that the count owes its own unresolved account of zero-point energy; add a post-1998 citation for the measured Λ.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Two components are real and verified. The citation defect is confirmed: Weinberg 1989 [15] predates the 1998 measurement of Lambda; his figure against the then-available bound was ~10^118, and the modern 10^123 (verified: Planck^4 / measured rho_Lambda = 10^122.9) requires a post-1998 observational citation. And the paragraph as written is under-argued against exactly this attack — 'cut off only at the Planck scale' concedes the computed number belongs to a truncated census without saying why the count escapes the truncated bill. BUT the central discrimination claim fails against the paper's actual position. The attack asserts the paper 'endorses a depth-66 ledger as physical': it does not — the abstract and Corollary 1 call 66 octaves 'the entire conceivable ladder,' Corollary 2 says nature occupies a few octaves and collider physics sixteen, and a Planck-depth census of a Hubble region (depth ~202) exceeds even the universe's holographic budget (depth 136) on the paper's own numbers. On Axioms M/S an unfunded level is not instantiated and carries no energy; the catastrophe is precisely the attribution of actual gravitating zero-point energy to every conceivable level regardless of funding — the surplus commitment in its purest form. The attack's correct 10^44-at-confinement-scale arithmetic cuts the same way: attributing gravitating hbar-omega/2 to unexcited conceivable modes fails at ANY depth, which is the count's point, not its debt (and the Casimir/Lamb effects are recoverable without vacuum energy, per R. L. Jaffe's source-interaction analysis). The exhibit survives, repaired; 'retire the exhibit' is overreach.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Rewrite the §9 sentence: 'the zero-point energy attributed to the mode family — cut off, charitably, at the Planck scale, since uncut the attribution diverges outright — exceeds the measured vacuum energy density by a factor of order 10^123 [15, +Riess et al. 1998 / Perlmutter et al. 1999 or Planck 2018] — machine-verified in the accompanying suite. The bill is not the count's: on Axioms M and S an unfunded level is not instantiated and carries no energy, and the catastrophe is precisely the attribution of actual energy to every conceivable level regardless of funding — the surplus commitment stated as an energy density. (Weinberg's contemporaneous figure, against the then-available observational bound, was near 10^118; the measured Lambda fixes the modern number.)' Apply the same 'attributed' framing to the abstract's clause. Optionally add one sentence acknowledging the count owes its own account of Casimir and Lamb, citing the source-interaction derivations that deliver them without vacuum energy.

batch_verdicts.quote: equipartition over the actually-infinite mode family predicts divergent radiated energy, measurement contradicts it, and the resolution was Planck's count [14] — the infinite retired from the physics, the count installed, and quantum mechanics founded in the act.
batch_verdicts.attack: Misdescribes the resolution. Planck quantized the energy exchanged per mode; he did not finitize the mode family. QED — the successor theory — retains infinitely many cavity modes per bounded region and reproduces the blackbody spectrum exactly: the UV suppression comes from the Boltzmann factor acting on quantized level spacings, not from truncating the mode census. What measurement refuted was classical equipartition, not 'infinitely many modes in a bounded region' — examined closely, the exhibit shows the infinite-mode commitment surviving and triumphing empirically once equipartition is replaced. 'The infinite retired from the physics' is false as history and as physics. Together with the vacuum-catastrophe finding, both of §9's historical exhibits — the paper's entire empirical case that the infinite-modes commitment has been 'historically refuted' (Introduction, claim Third) — fail.
batch_verdicts.fix: Restate accurately (Planck removed equipartition by quantizing exchange; the mode family survives in QED) and rebuild the exhibit around what it can actually carry — per-mode energy discreteness as the count's first victory — or retire the 'twice catastrophic' framing.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: The history and physics of the attack are correct: Planck quantized the energy exchanged per mode and did not finitize the mode family; QED retains infinitely many cavity modes per bounded region and reproduces the blackbody spectrum exactly, with UV suppression from the Boltzmann factor on quantized levels; so 'the infinite retired from the physics' is false as written and the sentence must change. BUT the conclusion — that the exhibit shows the infinite-mode commitment 'surviving and triumphing' and therefore fails — is overstated, because what Planck's law says is exactly that the unfunded tail contributes nothing: at temperature T the physically ACTIVE census is finite, modes the thermal budget cannot fund do not participate, and the mode list survives only as bookkeeping — which is precisely the paper's notation-versus-instantiated-structure distinction, in thermal dress. What measurement refuted was the claim that the whole conceivable census is physically active (equipartition = every mode carries kT); the recast exhibit carries the paper's thesis on accurate history, and Planck's own derivation was literally a combinatorial count of finite energy elements. The 'both exhibits fail, entire empirical case collapses' coda also inherits the overreach of the vacuum-catastrophe finding, ruled PARTIAL above. Real defect in the sentence; the exhibit is salvageable, not retirable.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Replace the §9 sentence: 'equipartition over the actually-infinite mode family — every conceivable mode physically active, each carrying kT — predicts divergent radiated energy; measurement contradicts it; and the resolution was Planck's count [14]: energy exchanged in discrete elements, counted combinatorially, so that modes the thermal budget cannot fund do not participate. The mode family survived as bookkeeping — the quantized theory keeps the full list and reproduces the spectrum exactly — but the claim that the whole conceivable census is physically active retired that year, the active census became finite, and quantum mechanics was founded in the act.' Adjust the Introduction's 'Third' and the §9 lead-in from 'the infinite-modes commitment has yielded an indirect observable consequence' to 'the attribution of physical activity (there, kT per mode; later, zero-point energy) to the entire unfunded census has yielded...' so both exhibits indict the same, accurately named, commitment.

batch_verdicts.quote: the lightest excitation of the pure gauge theory is the scalar glueball near 1.7 GeV [11], and no massless gauge excitation has ever appeared, on the instrument or in nature. Every physical probe that has ever interrogated the strong spectrum has found it gapped.
batch_verdicts.attack: The photon is a massless gauge excitation and it appears in nature constantly; the 'or in nature' clause breaks the pure-SU(3) scope of the sentence's first half, and no pure-gauge SU(3) sector exists in nature to be probed at all. Behind it sits a second conflation: the natural strong spectrum's lightest state is the pion, whose 135 MeV owes to explicit chiral symmetry breaking by quark masses — not to the Yang–Mills gap mechanism the prize asks about (in the chiral limit the pion is massless while the pure-gauge gap persists) — and glueballs have never been unambiguously identified in experiment (the f₀(1710) assignment remains contested). So 'found it gapped' in nature is true but is not evidence about the pure-YM gap, and 'no massless gauge excitation... in nature' is simply false as written. §12 scopes the identical claim correctly ('a massless excitation of the pure gauge sector'), proving the correct wording was available.
batch_verdicts.fix: Rescope: 'no massless excitation of the strong sector has ever appeared, on the instrument or in nature'; separate the natural gap (pion, quark-mass origin) from the pure-gauge gap explicitly, and note the glueball's experimental status honestly.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: The defense fails on the load-bearing clause. Read literally, 'no massless gauge excitation has ever appeared, on the instrument or in nature' is falsified by the photon — a massless gauge excitation observed in nature constantly — and no contextual reading rescues 'or in nature,' since no pure-SU(3) sector exists in nature to be probed at all: the clause cannot do work for the pure-gauge gap under any scoping. The paper's own §12 ('a massless excitation of the pure gauge sector') proves the correct wording was available, which makes the §7 version indefensible sloppiness in a prosecution brief that prizes exactness. The chiral-limit point is also correct and relevant: the natural spectrum's gap is carried by the pion at 135 MeV, whose mass owes to explicit chiral breaking by quark masses — in the chiral limit the pion is massless while the pure-gauge gap persists — so 'found it gapped' in nature, though true, is not evidence about the pure-YM gap mechanism the prize names, and the paragraph elides the two. One prong overreaches: the glueball-status demand attacks a claim the paper does not make — [11] is cited for the lattice instrument only, and no experimental glueball sighting is asserted — so an honest-status note is optional inoculation, not an owed correction. The sentence must change; the offered rescoping is the right one.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Replace the §7 Instrumental sentence with: 'the lightest excitation of the pure gauge theory is the scalar glueball near 1.7 GeV [11], and no massless excitation of the pure gauge sector has ever appeared on the instrument at any coupling or spacing. In nature the strong spectrum is gapped wherever it has been probed — its lightest state, the pion at 135 MeV, owes its mass to the explicit breaking of chiral symmetry by the quark masses, a mechanism distinct from the pure-gauge gap the problem statement names; the two facts are stated separately, and neither is asked to carry the other.' Optional inoculation: append '(the experimental identification of the glueball among the scalar mesons remains contested; the instrument's pure-gauge number does not depend on it).'

batch_verdicts.quote: the inverse coupling grows linearly in the octave count — the running coupling is, exactly, a meter that counts octaves, at the rate β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave
batch_verdicts.attack: 'Exactly' is false beyond one loop. The two-loop coefficient β₁ = 34N²/3 is nonzero and scheme-independent, so 1/g² is not linear in the octave count in any scheme; the per-octave increments are measurably unequal, and the running of α_s has been experimentally verified with four-loop precision. Lemma 1 carries the qualifier ('the one-loop inverse coupling') but the abstract and §6 ('the statement that physics advances by equal increments of 1/g² per doubling of scale') drop it at exactly the two places where the rhetorical weight — 'the theory's own deepest equation counts' — is placed. A phenomenologist referee reads the abstract's 'exactly' as not knowing two-loop running and stops there. The verified per-octave value 0.09657 is correct as one-loop arithmetic; the exactness claim is what fails.
batch_verdicts.fix: Insert 'at one loop' / 'to leading order' in the abstract and §6; if the octave-meter reading is to bear weight, state what the two-loop term does to it rather than suppressing it.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: No defense survives. The two-loop coefficient beta_1 = 34N^2/3 is nonzero and scheme-independent, so 1/g^2 is not linear in the octave count in any scheme; verified cold: at collider scales (g^2 ~ 1.48) the two-loop term is ~8.7% of the one-loop per-octave rate — the increments are unequal by an amount far exceeding the precision at which alpha_s running has been experimentally confirmed, so the abstract's 'exactly' is not merely formally but empirically false exactly where the meter has been read. The body's Lemma 1 carries the qualifier ('the one-loop inverse coupling'), and the pinned suite value 0.09657 = 11 ln2/(8 pi^2) is correct as one-loop arithmetic (verified), but the abstract and §1-Second/§6 drop the qualifier at the two places of maximum rhetorical weight ('the theory's own deepest equation counts'), promising an exactness the body correctly declines to deliver. The attempted defense — 'exactly' modifies the meter-identification, not the rate — dies on the adjacent clause 'at the rate beta_0 ln 2 / 8 pi^2 per octave,' which states a constant rate. The repair costs nothing: Lemma 1's actual work needs only monotone ascent with no finite-octave obstruction, which holds beyond one loop in the asymptotically free regime.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Abstract: 'the one-loop inverse coupling grows linearly in the octave count — the running coupling is, at leading order, a meter that counts octaves, at the rate beta_0 ln 2 / 8 pi^2 per octave, higher orders bending the rate without ever reversing the ascent.' §1-Second: 'the one-loop 1/g^2 advances by exactly beta_0 ln 2 / 8 pi^2 per octave of scale.' §6: 'the statement that, at leading order, physics advances by equal increments of 1/g^2 per doubling of scale — increments the higher orders correct and never halt.' Optionally add to Lemma 1's commentary: 'The two-loop term, scheme-independent, bends the meter's rate; it does not stop the climb — monotone ascent toward the free fixed point is all the argument uses.'

batch_verdicts.quote: the convergent cluster expansion of Osterwalder and Seiler establishes exponential clustering of correlations — a mass gap — together with the area law, for the Wilson theory at sufficiently strong coupling, for any compact gauge group, in any dimension [16]. On the counting side of the ledger, the gap is not a conjecture. It has been a theorem for fifty years.
batch_verdicts.attack: The paper's own clause 'for any compact gauge group' contains the counterexample that deflates the inference. The same theorem grants a mass gap and area law to compact U(1) at strong coupling — the photon's group — whose continuum physics is gapless and deconfined; Guth and Fröhlich–Spencer proved the weak-coupling Coulomb phase of 4D compact U(1), establishing that strong-coupling gaps are properties of the regulator regime that say nothing about the scaling window. So 'the gap has been a theorem for fifty years' is a theorem about the wrong phase: on the counting side of the ledger the gap is 'a theorem' for QED too, where nature's answer is no gap. The Rigorous leg of the three-part grading therefore carries no physical-gap content for the scaling window, and a lattice referee will say so; the entire physical weight falls on the Instrumental leg, which the paper elsewhere prices at (over-stated) percent precision.
batch_verdicts.fix: Add the compact-U(1) caveat explicitly and let the strong-coupling theorem carry only what it can: existence of gapped lattice phases, not evidence about the scaling-window gap. The grading structure survives; the 'not a conjecture — a theorem for fifty years' flourish does not.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: The physics of the attack is correct and the caveat is owed: Osterwalder–Seiler's strong-coupling expansion does grant the identical gap and area law to compact U(1) — whose weak-coupling 4D continuum physics is Coulombic and gapless (Guth 1980; Fröhlich–Spencer 1982) — so the strong-coupling theorem is phase-bound and, taken alone, says nothing about the scaling window; the flourish 'the gap is not a conjecture. It has been a theorem for fifty years' trades on an ambiguity a lattice referee will puncture with exactly this counterexample. BUT the attack overstates by claiming the deflated inference is drawn. The paper's three-part grading is built to avoid it: §7 explicitly assigns the scaling window to the Instrumental leg in the next paragraph, and every other statement of the claim — abstract, Introduction, §10, §12 — scopes 'by theorem' with 'at strong coupling' and 'by instrument' with 'in the window.' The Rigorous leg is offered as a contrast with the continuum side's zero theorems, not as scaling-window evidence, so 'the Rigorous leg carries no physical-gap content for the window' attacks a weight the paper never places there. (The aside that Instrumental precision is 'over-stated' is marginal: the scalar glueball 1730(50)(80) MeV is few-percent.) Real repair: add the U(1) caveat and temper the flourish so the phase-boundedness is stated by the paper before a referee states it.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: After the [16] citation in §7 Rigorous, insert: 'The theorem is deliberately phase-bound and group-blind: compact U(1) receives the identical strong-coupling gap and area law, while its weak-coupling continuum physics is Coulombic and gapless (Guth; Fröhlich–Spencer) — which is exactly why this section grades the scaling-window gap separately and prices it on the instrument, where the non-abelian theory, unlike U(1), exhibits no intervening deconfining transition.' Then temper the flourish: 'On the counting side of the ledger the gap is, in the strong-coupling phase, not a conjecture but a fifty-year theorem; what the theorem does not reach — the window where the physics lives — is graded next, on the instrument.' Add Guth (Phys. Rev. D 21, 2291 (1980)) and Fröhlich–Spencer (Commun. Math. Phys. 83, 411 (1982)) to the references.

batch_verdicts.quote: The lattice theory's observables converge to their scaling-window values with corrections vanishing as powers of the spacing; the instrument record of Section 6 is precisely the demonstration that at feasible spacings the lattice values already sit inside experiment's intervals.
batch_verdicts.attack: This is labeled 'Theorem 3' and given a '∎', but the proof's first load-bearing sentence is an empirical claim, not mathematics: power-law scaling of lattice artifacts is Symanzik-effective-theory lore plus numerical observation, and rigorous convergence of lattice gauge observables to a continuum limit is precisely the open problem the paper is about. The proof's second sentence cites 'the instrument record' — citing data inside a proof. Moreover the theorem's hypothesis, 'If the continuum gauge theory is consistent with O,' quantifies over an object §6 flatly says does not exist ('because the continuum construction does not exist'), making the hypothesis ill-defined on the paper's own account. Contrast NS Theorem 3, which had a genuine proof from proven convergence of discretizations to smooth solutions on a bounded window. Calling this a theorem is exactly the 'is proved' overclaim the register forbids, and a mathematician referee will strike the label.
batch_verdicts.fix: Either recast the hypothesis so it is well-posed without the continuum object (e.g., 'any predictive scheme whose finite-precision outputs are limits of lattice values as the spacing shrinks') and downgrade the label to Proposition with the empirical premise flagged as such, or prove the statement for a class of observables where convergence is actually a theorem.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Defense attempted and fails. Strongest defenses: (a) the hypothesis 'If the continuum gauge theory is consistent with O' can be read as a dialectical conditional over the opponent's asserted object — conditionals over unproven objects are standard mathematics, so the attack's 'ill-defined' prong is overstated; (b) the instrument-record citation could be read as illustrative rather than load-bearing. Neither saves the 'Theorem ... Proof ... ∎' register. The proof's first sentence — lattice observables converge to scaling-window values with power-law corrections — is Symanzik effective-theory lore plus numerical observation, not a theorem; rigorous continuum convergence of 4D lattice gauge observables is precisely the open problem the paper is about. The proof's second sentence cites experimental agreement data inside a proof. And as written the proof never logically connects its hypothesis to its conclusion: it argues lattice values sit inside experiment's intervals directly from the Section 6 record, leaving the stated continuum-consistency hypothesis idle. I verified the NS comparison: NS Theorem 3's hypothesis ('bounded region ... on which the flow is smooth') makes convergence of standard discretizations a genuine theorem of numerical analysis, so the contrast is fair. The paper's own Section 7 grading ladder (Rigorous vs Instrumental) condemns claiming theorem-grade for an instrument-grade premise; a mathematician referee will strike the label. Real defect, must change.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Downgrade and recondition. Replace the heading with '**Proposition 3 (conditional): Observational indistinguishability**' and the statement with: '*Let O be any finite set of observations of strong-interaction physics, each of finite precision. Suppose (i) the continuum formulation, as its practitioners deploy it, assigns each observed quantity a value inside its interval, and (ii) the lattice observables converge to those values as the spacing shrinks — the scaling property every lattice computation assumes, verified on the instrument at percent precision (Section 6) but delivered by no theorem, that absence being Section 8's subject. Then a lattice theory of sufficiently fine spacing is consistent with O.*' Replace the proof with one that is actually a proof from the stated hypotheses: '*Proof.* Finite precision means each observation constrains its quantity to an open interval; convergence into an open interval is eventual membership; choose the depth so every observed quantity's lattice value has entered its interval. The resulting theory has finitely many degrees of freedom in any bounded region and is consistent with O. ∎' Append one grading sentence: 'Hypothesis (ii) is instrument-grade — the same grade as Section 7's middle leg — and the conclusion inherits it.' Corollary 5 must then read 'on the scaling hypothesis, the surplus entails no finite-precision observable consequence' — the unfalsifiability verdict carries the same conditional, stated rather than hidden.

batch_verdicts.quote: the running coupling is, exactly, a meter that counts octaves, at the rate β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave
batch_verdicts.attack: False as stated: the inverse coupling is linear in the octave count at one loop only. The universal two-loop term adds a log-of-log, higher orders are scheme-dependent, and every QFT referee knows it. Lemma 1 in the body carries the qualifier ('the one-loop inverse coupling grows linearly'), but the abstract's 'exactly' and §6's unqualified 'physics advances by equal increments of 1/g² per doubling of scale' both drop it — the abstract promises an exactness the body correctly does not deliver. A false 'exactly' about the field's most famous equation, in the abstract, triggers immediate credibility discount; the test suite pins only the one-loop statement, so the manuscript's headline claim outruns its own mechanical pin.
batch_verdicts.fix: Insert 'at one loop' in the abstract and §6 ('the one-loop running coupling is, exactly, a meter that counts octaves'), and optionally note that higher orders bend but do not stop the ascent — which is all Lemma 1 needs.
batch_verdicts.reasoning: Defense attempted and fails on all three lines. (a) Reading 'exactly' as 'literally is a meter' rather than 'exactly linear' — fails, because the same abstract sentence opens 'the inverse coupling grows linearly in the octave count' and pins a constant rate 'β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave'; constancy of the rate is the one-loop-only claim. (b) Dismissing higher orders as scheme artifacts — fails: β₁ = 34N²/3 = 102 for pure SU(3) is scheme-independent, so the nonlinearity is physical fact, not convention. (c) Claiming Lemma 1's body qualifier ('the one-loop inverse coupling') covers the abstract and §6 — fails: abstracts are read standalone, §1 and §6 also drop the qualifier ('advances by exactly β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave of scale'; 'equal increments of 1/g² per doubling of scale'), and the qualifier's presence in Lemma 1 proves the authors knew better, which makes the omission rhetorical drift — the exact register defect charged. Cold-verified: one-loop per-octave increment 0.096567 (matches the finding's 0.09657 and the suite's pin, whose own docstring says 'one loop, pure SU(3)' — so the mechanical pin covers only the qualified claim); two-loop increments computed by numerical integration deviate from constancy by 18.4% at α_s = 0.3 and 8.1% at α_s = 0.118 — measurably unequal exactly where the running is experimentally verified to four loops. The repair costs the argument nothing: Lemma 1 needs only monotone ascent to the free fixed point, which two-loop pure Yang–Mills preserves (β₁ > 0). Real defect in the abstract, §1, and §6; must change.
batch_verdicts.fix_v: Three insertions, exact language. Abstract: replace 'the inverse coupling grows linearly in the octave count — the running coupling is, exactly, a meter that counts octaves, at the rate β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave' with 'at one loop the inverse coupling grows linearly in the octave count — the running coupling is a meter that counts octaves, at the leading rate β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave, higher orders retuning the increment without arresting the ascent'. §1 Second claim: replace '1/g² advances by exactly β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave of scale' with 'at one loop 1/g² advances by exactly β₀ ln 2 / 8π² per octave of scale, and higher loops adjust the increment without ever halting it'. §6: replace 'the statement that physics advances by equal increments of 1/g² per doubling of scale' with 'the statement that, to leading order, physics advances by equal increments of 1/g² per doubling of scale — the higher-loop terms retune the meter; they do not stop it counting'. Optionally add one sentence to Lemma 1's discussion noting β₁ = 34N²/3 > 0 for pure SU(N), so the two-loop flow still ascends monotonically — all the lemma needs.

inline_verdicts.quote: One full second of proton time funds a depth of **26**. … the Lloyd budget of the observable universe, 10¹²⁰ operations, reaches depth **132**
inline_verdicts.attack: Neither number follows from the paper's own Theorem 1. The process clause defines the fundable depth as N*ₚ ≤ log₁₆(30ET/πℏ + 1) − 1; for one proton-second (2ET/πℏ = 9.07×10²³ ops) this gives 20.87 − 1 = 19.87 → depth 19, and for 10¹²⁰ ops it gives 100.6 − 1 = 99.6 → depth 99. The printed 26 and 132 are exactly the base-8 census-priced depths floor(log₈(7·ops + 1) − 1) = 26.47 and 132.86 — i.e. the demand D(N) = (8^(N+1)−1)/7 at one operation per cell, which is the *Navier–Stokes paper's* Theorem 1 formula (its Corollary 1 prints the identical sentence '…~10¹²⁰ operations, reaches depth 132', correctly under that paper's own demand). This paper sharpened the process demand to U(N) = (16^(N+1)−1)/15 but imported the old census-priced numbers. The state-side values in the same corollary (depth 1 from 36 bits, depth 136 from 10¹²³ bits) DO follow the stated state clause, so the asymmetry is not interpretive charity — the process pair was computed with the wrong base. The contradiction is visible within the abstract alone: it states the update demand is (16^(N+1)−1)/15 per crossing, yet 'one second of proton time funds twenty-six octaves' — one update of depth 26 costs (16²⁷−1)/15 ≈ 2.2×10³¹ operations, about 2.4×10⁷ times the proton's stated one-second budget of 9.1×10²³. A referee who recomputes the showcase numbers from the displayed formula gets 19 and 99, then reads 'All values are machine-verified' and concludes the suite pins a formula the theorem does not state. For a paper whose entire brand is that the counting is elementary and exact, this is the single most damaging checkable defect.
inline_verdicts.fix: Either (a) recompute with the theorem's own meter and print 19 and 99 (both still logarithmic; the thesis is unchanged and in fact strengthened), or (b) explicitly define the second process meter — construction of the census once, D(N) ≤ 2ET/πℏ, with its own displayed bound N ≤ log₈(14ET/πℏ + 1) − 1 — label 26 and 132 as construction depths, and give the sustained-update depths 19 and 99 alongside. Update the abstract's 'twenty-six' and 'one hundred thirty-two' to match whichever choice is made, and make the test suite pin the same formula the theorem displays.
inline_verdicts.adjudicator: the author-engine inline, cold-verified where arithmetic

inline_verdicts.section: §8 · Why the continuum cannot decide its own question
inline_verdicts.quote: The scaling limit exists; the axioms are satisfied; and the interaction did not survive the completion.
inline_verdicts.attack: This attributes to [19] content the theorem does not contain. ADC prove that all subsequential scaling limits are Gaussian; the theorem neither establishes convergence to a unique limit (the logarithmically-corrected normalization at the 4D critical point is exactly the delicate open issue) nor verifies the Wightman/OS axioms for any limit object. 'The scaling limit exists; the axioms are satisfied' is therefore a misstatement of the cited result — a small one, since a Gaussian limit point trivially satisfies the axioms once pinned, but a constructive-QFT referee reads it as evidence the authors have not read the theorem they lean on.
inline_verdicts.fix: Replace with: 'every subsequential scaling limit is Gaussian — in no limit point does the interaction survive'; drop the axiom clause or source it separately to the free-field literature.
