inline_verdicts.section: §9 · The epistemic status of the continuum (also Abstract and §1)
inline_verdicts.quote: The first is the classical cavity: equipartition over the actually-infinite mode family predicts divergent radiated energy, measurement contradicts it, and the resolution was Planck's count [14] — the infinite retired from the physics, the count installed, and quantum mechanics founded in the act.
inline_verdicts.attack: This is the textbook myth of the ultraviolet catastrophe, stated as history with Planck 1901 as the citation. Planck's 1900-01 derivation was not a response to the equipartition divergence: he did not accept equipartition, the Rayleigh-Jeans law played no role in his route (Wien's law plus resonator entropy did), and the 'catastrophe' was named and pressed by Ehrenfest in 1911 — Kuhn's Black-Body Theory and the Quantum Discontinuity (1978) is the standard demolition of the causal story told here. The predecessor NS paper worded this correctly ('arrived at from the infrared data before the catastrophe had even been stated in full: the count preceded the complete diagnosis'); this paper drops that guard and asserts the false ordering flatly, three times (abstract: 'refuted by measurement and resolved by Planck's count'; §1; §9). The physics point (continuum equipartition diverges, quantized counting does not) is untouched; the historical attribution is the defect.
inline_verdicts.fix: Restore the NS paper's careful ordering, or recite: divergence made explicit by Rayleigh (1900) and named by Ehrenfest (1911), Planck's count in place before the diagnosis was complete — citing Rayleigh/Ehrenfest alongside [14].
inline_verdicts.adjudicator: the author-engine inline, cold-verified where arithmetic

inline_verdicts.section: §9 · The epistemic status of the continuum
inline_verdicts.quote: The second is the quantum vacuum itself: the zero-point energy of the continuum mode family, cut off only at the Planck scale, exceeds the observed vacuum energy density by a factor of order 10¹²³ [15] — machine-verified in the accompanying suite — the largest quantitative discrepancy between a theoretical expectation and a measurement in the history of science.
inline_verdicts.attack: Citation mismatch: [15] is Weinberg's 1989 review, which predates the 1998 discovery of nonzero vacuum energy; Weinberg compares against an observational upper bound and his figure is ~118-120 orders. The 10¹²³ the test suite computes ((1.22×10¹⁹ GeV / 2.24×10⁻¹² GeV)⁴ ≈ 8.8×10¹²²) requires the measured dark-energy scale, for which no post-1998 source is cited. Secondarily, the sentence's own qualifier 'cut off only at the Planck scale' concedes the catastrophic number is computed on a FINITE mode census (about 66 octaves on the paper's own ladder, Corollary 1), so a referee will ask why a divergence the paper books to 'the actually-infinite mode family' (Corollary 5's framing, 'the infinite-modes commitment') is exhibited by a cutoff calculation a finite-depth theory shares — the attribution needs one honest sentence, or the second 'catastrophe' exhibit weakens.
inline_verdicts.fix: Cite a post-1998 measurement (e.g., Planck 2018 cosmological parameters, or Martin 2012) alongside [15] for the observed value; add a sentence acknowledging the estimate is cutoff-based and stating why the paper still assigns the liability to the continuum's zero-point commitment rather than to mode-counting as such.
inline_verdicts.adjudicator: the author-engine inline, cold-verified where arithmetic

inline_verdicts.quote: One full second of proton time funds a depth of 26.
inline_verdicts.attack: Inconsistent with Theorem 1's own process clause. The theorem prices fundable depth by the update demand U(N): N*ₚ = log₁₆(30ET/πℏ + 1) − 1, which for a proton-second gives 19.9, not 26; for the Lloyd budget ('10¹²⁰ operations, reaches depth 132') it gives 99.6, not 132. The corollary's 26 and 132 come from applying the 8-count census D(N) to the operation supply — one op per cell, a single construction — and the test suite silently switches to log₈ (test_proton_one_second_depth, test_universe_depths) rather than using the theorem's formula. The conclusions survive (all depths remain finite and logarithmic) but a referee who checks the corollary against the theorem's displayed bound gets different numbers, in a paper whose banner is that every exact claim is machine-pinned.
inline_verdicts.fix: Either recompute the corollary with N*ₚ (19 and 99), or state explicitly that these two entries price a single construction of the census (8-meter) rather than the sustained native-frequency update the theorem's process clause prices, and add the distinction to the test suite.

inline_verdicts.quote: the gap stands at percent precision: the lightest excitation of the pure gauge theory is the scalar glueball near 1.7 GeV [11]
inline_verdicts.attack: Precision inflation. Morningstar–Peardon's scalar glueball is 1730(50)(80) MeV — 5.5% combined error, not 'percent precision'; and BMW 2008's light-hadron masses carry total uncertainties of typically 2–4% (the collaboration's own gloss is agreement 'within 3% or less'), so §6's 'at percent precision' is also a stretch. The house rigor-ledger has flagged precision overstatement before ('ppm overstatement'); a lattice referee will read 'percent precision' as 1% and check. The 1.7 GeV attribution itself is correct and well-cited.
inline_verdicts.fix: Use 'few-percent precision' in all four occurrences (abstract twice, §6, §7), and consider quoting 1730(50)(80) MeV directly — the paper's own candor standard is better served by the actual error bars.
inline_verdicts.adjudicator: the author-engine inline, cold-verified where arithmetic

inline_verdicts.quote: These are the same telescopes, cell for cell, as the cascade census of the fluid paper [4]: the octree of a bounded region does not care whether its levels are eddies or field modes.
inline_verdicts.attack: The plural is false as a citation claim. The fluid paper contains only the 8-ary census telescope (8^(N+1)−1)/7; the 16-ary update telescope (16^(N+1)−1)/15 appears nowhere in it (a search of the NS manuscript finds no occurrence of any 16-power sum). A referee checking the cross-reference finds one of the two 'same telescopes' was never in [4], and — combined with the finding above — will infer that the update telescope was bolted on without propagating it through the corollary's numbers, which is precisely what happened.

inline_verdicts.quote: The ladder from the confinement scale to the Planck scale — the entire conceivable range of the theory — spans **65.7 octaves**; experimentally verified quantum chromodynamics occupies **16**
inline_verdicts.attack: Three significant figures are quoted with no inputs stated anywhere in the manuscript. 65.7 reproduces only with Λ_conf = 200 MeV and E_Planck = 1.221×10¹⁹ GeV (log₂ gives 65.73); with the equally standard MS-bar Λ_QCD^(nf=3) ≈ 332 MeV the ladder is 65.0, and with 1 GeV it is 63.4 — the second significant figure is convention-dependent. Likewise '16' requires the unstated endpoint 13 TeV (log₂(13 TeV/200 MeV) = 15.99). A referee attempting reproduction from the text alone cannot recover 65.7 without guessing the author's conventions, which undercuts the manuscript's own reproducibility standard ('All values are machine-verified' — verified against inputs the reader is never shown).
inline_verdicts.fix: State the inputs inline: 'taking the confinement scale at 200 MeV, the Planck energy 1.22×10¹⁹ GeV, and the collider frontier at 13 TeV' — one clause suffices.
